reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an unofficial music remix and a channel distributing downloadable electronic music. The donation request is described as voluntary support for music quality, production time, livestream infrastructure, and studio expenses, rather than an investment, guaranteed return, or request for credentials. The blurred frames add limited context but do not establish a separate deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: Donate & Support my channel for new futures
Need money, for better music quality, more free time to dig new, better, music and 24/7 livestream radio server and other special expensive things, like studio for live sets

opening.argument: Judge, consider the sequence presented to viewers: a free download is offered through an external SoundCloud link, and the same description asks for financial support. The offer can draw viewers away from the video toward a separate destination, where the appeal for support is part of the surrounding pitch. The evidence does not establish what happens after a viewer follows the link, but it does establish an easy-to-obtain digital reward paired with a requested viewer action. That pairing deserves more weight than the music title alone.

citations.quote: Donate & Support my channel for new futures: LT274010051004626228 Edgaras Butenis.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the title identifies a remix, but that does not resolve the viewer-facing solicitation in its description. Nor does calling the request voluntary answer why the download is introduced as “Download & Support.” This argument does not require a guaranteed return or a credentials request: it concerns whether a free digital item is being used to steer viewers to an external link alongside an appeal for money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted text does not make a donation a condition of downloading. It explicitly calls the offering a “Free Download,” while separately asking for support and explaining proposed channel expenses. A link to a music download plus an optional donation request is not evidence of a deceptive claim flow or an unusually easy reward contingent on payment.

citations.quote: Need money, for better music quality, more free time to dig new, better, music and 24/7 livestream radio server

opening.argument: Judge, the concern is the combination, not any single phrase. The description presents a free download, sends viewers to an external SoundCloud address, and supplies bank details for donations. It also describes future improvements as the reason money is needed. None of those statements verifies how contributions would be used or what a viewer would encounter at the download destination. The free offer makes participation easy, while the direct payment details make the financial solicitation concrete; those signals warrant scrutiny even though the video itself is presented as music.

citations.quote: Donate & Support my channel for new futures: LT274010051004626228 Edgaras Butenis. Luminor|DNB SWIFT: AGBLLT2X
Need money, for better music quality, more free time to dig new, better, music and 24/7 livestream radio server

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the stated production expenses as an explanation of the donation request. They are the uploader's stated intentions, not evidence that contributions will produce those results. Likewise, the blurred frames may add little, but they cannot verify the external download or the payment appeal. The relevant evidence is in the description's combination of a free offer, an outbound link, and bank-transfer details.

citations.quote: Donate & Support my channel for new futures: LT274010051004626228 Edgaras Butenis. Luminor|DNB SWIFT: AGBLLT2X

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A request for donations and an external music link are not, by themselves, evidence of deception. The description says the music is free and gives ordinary channel-related reasons for seeking support. It does not promise a reward for transferring money, require payment to access the download, or claim that donors will receive a return. Unverified future plans are not enough to turn this music post into a scam.

citations.quote: Need money, for better music quality, more free time to dig new, better, music and 24/7 livestream radio server and other special expensive things, like studio for live sets

opening.argument: Judge, the remix is not the only purpose conveyed by this post. Its description introduces other channel projects, describes a free-download offer, asks viewers to support artists, and then asks them to donate to this channel through listed bank details. That progression turns the music presentation into a route for promoting the uploader's own destinations and funding request. The free download is the point of entry; the support appeal is the requested participation. The issue is whether the ordinary entertainment framing causes the judge to overlook that viewer-directed solicitation.

citations.quote: SUPPORT artist, Record Companies for those music GIFTS !! Donate & Support my channel for new futures: LT274010051004626228 Edgaras Butenis.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense establishes that this is a music upload; it does not establish that the description is solely about listening. The uploader also promotes channel projects and places a direct donation request beside the download offer. Calling those requests voluntary addresses compulsion, but not their promotional role in steering viewers from the remix toward further participation.

citations.quote: Donate & Support my channel for new futures

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion alone is not a scam. The title identifies an unofficial remix, and the description openly identifies the music channels, the free download, and the donation request. Nothing quoted makes the download conditional on donating or represents the donation as a way to obtain a reward. The prosecution has shown that the uploader promotes a music channel, not that the promotion is deceptive.
